items.title: How the US controls Iraq's oil revenues
items.description: US forces are set to withdraw on Wednesday from their last bases in Iraq, a departure celebrated as a victory by Iran and its allies, which have deep influence in the country where 4,500 Americans died during more than two decades of war. Still, since its 2003 invasion of Iraq , the US has held effective control of the country’s oil revenue dollars, giving Washington extraordinary leverage over Baghdad’s affairs, with implications for regional dynamics involving Iran. How does the US control Iraq’s oil revenues? This stems primarily from the management of Iraq’s oil income through the Federal Reserve Bank of New York. After the 2003 invasion, the Coalition Provisional Authority (CPA), led by the US, set up the Development Fund for Iraq (DFI), held at the New York Fed, and designed to collect the oil revenues for use in reconstruction and development efforts. A US Marine watches a woman and her child during a series of raids to hunt arms and guerrilla suspects south of Baghdad, Iraq on December 1, 2004. —Reuters/File The Fund also aimed to protect the Iraqi oil revenues from lawsuits and claims relating to Saddam Hussein’s rule. An executive order by then president George W. Bush to set up the arrangement has been renewed by every president since. The DFI eventually became an account of the Central Bank of Iraq at the New York Federal Reserve, as it remains today. What leverage does this give the US over Iraq? Oil is Iraq’s most important revenue source, making up about 90 per cent of the state budget. This gives Washington significant sway over the country’s economic and political stability. When the Iraqi government asked US troops to leave in 2020, Washington reportedly threatened to cut Iraq’s access to the New York Federal Reserve funds, with Baghdad ultimately backing down. A US army tank takes up a position near the scene of a suicide bomb attack in Baghdad, Iraq on July 14, 2005. —Reuters/File While Iraq has gained more control over its financial affairs since the early years of the occupation, the link highlights the enduring influence of the US on the economic landscape of Iraq, even as the latter seeks to assert sovereignty and independence. Why has the arrangement endured for so long? The system helped anchor Iraq’s financial stability and safeguards state finances, government officials told Reuters on condition of anonymity. It boosts international confidence in the management of oil income, eases access to US dollars needed for trade and imports, and protects revenues from external claims and financial shocks, including claims by creditors and lawsuits, they said. A giant Iraqi flag hangs off the reconstructed 12th century “Hadba” leaning minaret at the historic Great Mosque of al-Nuri in the old city of Mosul on September 29, 2026 as Iraq marks the withdrawal of the US-led anti-Islamic State coalition forces from the country. —AFP The arrangement supports exchange-rate stability and underpins confidence in the Iraqi economy, while working to strengthen domestic financial institutions and assert greater economic sovereignty, they added. It also allows the government to push back against some actors, such as Iran-allied groups, who seek fewer curbs on dollar access. Last year, the US imposed sanctions on Iraqi banks and individuals it accused of laundering money for Iran. How has this arrangement affected Iraq? The heavy curbs on US dollar supply led to a parallel, informal market for dollars, resulting in a price spread between the official exchange rate set by the central bank and that on the black market. The price difference is essentially a risk premium for dealing outside the formal system. In his second term, President Donald Trump has pursued a campaign of maximum pressure on Iran , with Iraq often caught in the crossfire as Tehran has used it as a vital economic lung. The war he launched with Israel against Iran on February 28 added further pressure on Baghdad. What is the status of Iraq’s oil revenue management? Iraqi oil revenues remain in the custody of the Federal Reserve Bank of New York. CBI has historically used dollar auctions, formally known as the foreign currency window, as the main mechanism to supply dollars. Private banks and exchange houses could bid daily to purchase US dollars using Iraqi dinars. Iraq formally ended the auction system at the start of 2025 after significant US pressure, part of a broad crackdown on alleged siphoning of dollars to sanctioned parties, especially Iran. Header image: A stage with a banner for Sovereignty Day in Baghdad, Iraq on September 30, 2026. —Reuters

items.title: Hausse des cancers en Algérie : le constat glaçant du Pr Senhadji
items.description: Les chiffres font froid dans le dos et le constat est glaçant. Selon le Professeur Kamel Sanhadji, président de l’Agence nationale de sécurité sanitaire (ANSS), l’Algérie enregistre chaque année, entre 14 000 et 15 000 nouveaux cas de cancers qui viennent s’ajouter aux 56 000 malades qui existent déjà. Un constat qui glace les sangs et soulève des interrogations quant à l’origine de cette inquiétante propagation et aux moyens de freiner la progression exponentielle des cancers dans notre pays. En Algérie, l’Agence nationale de sécurité sanitaire (ANSS) a été créée en juin 2020. Son rôle est essentiellement stratégique et scientifique puisque cette institution aide l’Etat à anticiper, prévenir et gérer les risques pouvant menacer la santé de la population. Son président, le Professeur Kamel Sanhadji tire la sonnette d’alarme. Dans une vidéo mise en ligne par Santé Plus, le Professeur se montre particulièrement alarmant. « Même si vous construisez des centres, même si vous achetez tous les médicaments que vous voulez, ça ne va pas suffire parce que le nombre de personnes touchées par le cancer progresse chaque année de 14 000 ou 15 000 cas supplémentaires qui viennent s’ajouter aux 56 000 malades existants déjà, et là on va vite atteindre 80 000, 90 000, 100 000 malades », a-t-il déclaré. Médicaments anticancer : jusqu’à 3000 euros pour une seule boîte Professeur Sanhadji souligne l’insuffisance des hôpitaux pouvant accueillir les cancéreux ainsi que la cherté du traitement. « Où les mettre ? C’est impossible de les traiter et de leur acheter les médicaments. Les traitements pour le cancer sont très chers : il faut compter entre 1000 et 3000 euros la boite, pour une prise en charge en continu. Comment les gens vont-ils faire ? » interroge-t-il, et rappelle : « Je suis conseiller auprès du président Tebboune qui est au courant de cette situation. Il a beau donner l’argent et mettre de grands moyens, on n’y arrivera pas ! » Le président Tebboune peut « mettre tous les budgets de l’Etat dans le traitement du cancer, cela ne suffira pas », martèle-t-il. Il ne faut pas faire de cancer ! Et lorsque les journalistes lui demandent quelle serait la solution, le président de l’Agence nationale de sécurité sanitaire répond : « Il n’y a pas de secret, il ne faut pas faire de cancer. » Dans son message, le Pr Senhadji souligne la nécessité de « s’attaquer aux causes d’exposition aux cancers (alimentation, tabac, surpoids et obésité, manque d’activité physique…). « C’est cela la vraie prévention basée sur des données solides », a-t-il dit. Face à l’évolution de cette maladie en Algérie, « l’enjeu n’est plus seulement d’augmenter les capacités de traitement, mais d’agir en amont sur les facteurs de risque, de favoriser le diagnostic précoce et de garantir un parcours de soins plus accessible et mieux coordonné », soutient le Pr Senhadji. Les cancers progressent de manière préoccupante en Algérie. Selon les données citées par l’OMS et les spécialistes algériens : le cancer du sein est le plus fréquent chez les femmes alors que le cancer colorectal, de la prostate et des poumons sont les plus courants. Les experts imputent cette explosion à plusieurs facteurs comme le vieillissement de la population, le tabagisme, la sédentarité, une alimentation déséquilibrée et la pollution environnementale. Ils préconisent la mise en place d’une stratégie nationale de prévention, de dépistage précoce et de surveillance sanitaire pour contenir la progression de la maladie. L’article Hausse des cancers en Algérie : le constat glaçant du Pr Senhadji est apparu en premier sur TSA .

items.title: 3 terrorists killed in IBO in KP's Mir Ali: state media
items.description: Security forces killed three terrorists in an intelligence-based operation in the Mir Ali area of Khyber Pakhtunkhwa’s North Waziristan district, state broadcaster PTV reported on Wednesday, citing security sources. The sources added that hideouts of the Fitna al Khawarij were targeted in Mir Ali and surrounding areas. Fitna al Khawarij is a term the state uses for terrorists belonging to the banned Tehreek-i-Taliban Pakistan (TTP). A large quantity of weapons and ammunition was recovered from the terrorists killed during the operation, security sources said. According to PTV , security forces also thwarted an attempt by the terrorists to intercept a ration truck near the Mir Ali Bazaar. It added that security forces were committed to the complete elimination of terrorism under the counter-terrorism campaign ‘Azm-e-Istehkam’. President Asif Ali Zardari and Prime Minister Shehbaz Sharif have lauded security forces for their successful operation in Mir Ali, Radio Pakistan reported. President Asif Ali Zardari said that the operation against terrorism would continue to ensure peace in the country, adding that the designs of the terrorists would be foiled at all costs. PM Shehbaz, meanwhile, held that eliminating terrorism remained the government’s top priority, according to state media. KP has been witnessing terrorist attacks and security challenges for a long time. The province, excluding the merged districts, recorded 54 terrorist attacks in August compared with 36 in July, representing an increase of 50 per cent, according to data compiled by the Pakistan Institute for Conflict and Security Studies (PICSS). A day earlier, in an IBO in KP’s Bara area, security forces killed five terrorists. On Monday, four terrorists were killed during an IBO in Dera Ismail Khan. Last week, a dozen people lost their lives while 35 others were injured in a suicide blast that targeted the Aman Mela police checkpost in DI Khan’s Darazinda tehsil. On Sept 18, a major attack in the old Police Lines in KP’s Kohat claimed 23 lives and injured about 100 others. Eight terrorists were killed during an overnight clearance operation . On Sept 17, security forces killed 10 terrorists in separate operations in KP between Sept 15 and 17. Earlier in the month, over 20 terrorists were killed during multiple engagements in KP between Sept 3 and 5.

items.title: Pakistan men’s squash team seal bronze and semi-final spot as women's campaign ends
items.description: Pakistan’s men’s squash team confirmed at least a bronze medal at the Asian Games on Wednesday, booking their semi-final spot with a straight-sets win over South Korea, while the women’s team saw their campaign end with a round-robin defeat to China at the Nagoya Kinjo Futo Arena. Pakistan’s men swept South Korea 2-0 in their quarter-final without needing a deciding rubber. Mohammad Ashab Irfan set the tone in the opening match against Na Jooyoung, needing all three games but rarely looking troubled. The 22-year-old traded early points with his 19-year-old opponent before surging to a 7-2 lead in the first game, eventually closing it out 11-5 in nine minutes. The second followed a similar script — Jooyoung twice clawed his way back to within a couple of points, only for Ashab to restore his cushion each time and seal it 11-8. The Korean threatened a fightback in the third, pulling back three points as Ashab served for the match, but the Pakistani finally converted on his fourth attempt to complete an 11-5, 11-8, 11-8 win in just under half an hour and put Pakistan 1-0 up. Pakistan’s top-ranked player, Noor Zaman, then had the chance to seal the tie against Seojin Oh, and made light work of it despite a scare in the third game. The world No. 33 raced through the first game 11-4 in six minutes and followed it with an equally comfortable 11-5 in the second, building leads of four points or more in both. Oh, 20, produced his best squash of the tie in the third, fighting back from 8-7 down to level and then snatching the game 11-8 to keep Korean hopes alive. But Noor responded immediately in the fourth, racing into a four-point lead and reeling off seven straight points to close it out 11-2 — sealing both the match and a 2-0 win for Pakistan without the tie needing to go the distance. Noor and Ashab have already secured bronze medal in the singles event. The result sends Pakistan through to face Hong Kong, who defeated Qatar in the other quarter-final, in Thursday’s semi-final. There was no such reward for Pakistan’s women, who went down 2-1 to China in their second round-robin qualifier — a defeat that followed an opening 3-0 loss to Macau in the same play-off group and ends their hopes of reaching the quarter-finals. Pakistan had finished third in their four-team pool behind Hong Kong and South Korea, dropping them into a round-robin decider against China and Macau for the tournament’s remaining two quarter-final berths. Wednesday’s tie followed the same pattern as their first: an early loss in the opening singles, a spirited fightback in the middle match, and a decider that ultimately slipped away. Thirteen-year-old Mahnoor Ali opened proceedings against Ziyi Liu and never found her rhythm. The 19-year-old Chinese player raced through the first game in five minutes, winning it 11-4, before edging a tighter second 11-8. Liu pulled away in the decider, building an early six-point cushion that Mahnoor could only intermittently interrupt, and closed out the match 11-2 to hand China a 1-0 lead in the tie. Sana Bahadar dragged Pakistan level with the standout performance of the day, overcoming Yuning Zhang in three hard-fought games. The 20-year-old built an early 7-2 cushion in the first before Zhang, also 20, rallied to within three points; Sana held her nerve to close it out 11-7 on her second match point. The second game swung repeatedly — the pair traded the lead seven times before Sana, trailing 9-6, reeled off three straight points to level at 9-9 and then closed it out 11-9. Any hope of a Chinese recovery in the third evaporated as Sana, after trading the opening two points, won eight in a row to seal the game 11-2 and level the tie at 1-1. The contest came down to a decider between 14-year-old Sehrish Ali and Ziyuan Yin, and China’s teenager proved too strong. Yin, 14, surged to an early lead in the first game and closed it out 11-3, then weathered a mid-game wobble in the second — Sehrish had narrowed the gap to 9-5 — before finishing it 11-7. The Pakistani teenager briefly led in the decider, but Yin responded with a burst of consecutive points to pull clear and served out the match 11-2, sealing a 2-1 win for China. At the Aichi Prefecture General Shooting Gallery, Pakistan’s Ghulam Mustafa Bashir sits eighth in the men’s 25m rapid fire pistol qualification after a strong opening stage on Wednesday. Bashir scored 289 with eight inner tens across his 30 shots, posting series scores of 95 (8 seconds), 96 (6 seconds) and 98 (4 seconds). The three-time Olympian, who won bronze at the 2022 ISSF World Championships in Cairo, now faces Stage 2 on Thursday — another 30 shots that will determine his final qualification score out of 600 and whether he advances to the final.

items.title: Swedish rights prize honours Pakistani human rights lawyer Jalila Haider
items.description: Human rights lawyer and activist Jalila Haider on Wednesday received the Right Livelihood prize, dubbed an “alternative Nobel”. The Sweden-based Right Livelihood Foundation honoured Haider “for breaking barriers, as the first female lawyer from her Hazara community , to challenge ethnic, state and patriarchal persecution, guided by the conviction that no human being is illegal.” According to the foundation’s website, Haider in 2018 “led a seven-day hunger strike against the targeted killing of Hazaras” that led to direct negotiations between the army chief and Hazara women, “resulting in a sustained decrease in attacks against the community”. It added that Haider had combined legal work with street activism and community empowerment, securing “justice for thousands targeted or ignored by those in power, specifically ethnic, gender and religious minorities, as well as refugees”. “Her law firm has also helped restore freedom of movement for more than 600 political activists and human rights defenders,” the Right Livelihood Foundation said. Haider is a founding member of the Women’s Democratic Front as well, the foundation said, adding that she “helped pioneer Balochistan’s first Women’s March, a street mobilisation that sparked discussions on feminism across the deeply patriarchal region”. Through her organisation ‘We the Humans’, Haider has “helped over 400 widows of terrorism victims gain financial independence”, the foundation said. “Despite detention, cyber-harassment and death threats, she continues to work towards a world where, in her words, ‘no human being is illegal’,” the foundation said. The Right Livelihood Award was established in 1980, when Swedish-German stamp collector Jakob von Uexkull sold part of his collection to fund it, after the foundation behind the Nobel Prizes refused to create new awards in the fields of environmental protection and international development. A prominent US artificial intelligence researcher and two women-led rights groups were also recognised. The jury said in a statement it had chosen US artificial intelligence researcher Timnit Gebru “for challenging concentrated power in artificial intelligence and pioneering digital technology rooted in justice, lived experience and human agency.” Gebru is known for her work examining how biases influence AI and in 2017, Gebru co-founded Black in AI. The foundation also gave the nod to the Rural Women’s Assembly — a grassroots movement of more than 178,000 small-scale farmers across 11 Southern African nations. The Georgian Young Lawyers’ Association (GYLA), which the jury described as “Georgia’s oldest and most prominent human rights organisation,” was also honoured.

items.title: Somali forces recover oil tanker carrying Pakistani crewmen over 5 months after hijacking by pirates
items.description: KARACHI: Somali maritime police said on Tuesday that they had recovered the MT Honour 25 — an oil tanker hijacked by armed pirates off the coast of Puntland on April 21 — amid reports of casualties among the crew. The Honour 25 — a Palau-flagged oil tanker — had 19 crew members on board, including 10 Pakistanis. “The naval and ground units of the Puntland Maritime Police Force conducted a planned operation in the Dharin-Bar area of Bandar Beyla district,” the maritime police said in its initial statement. In another late-night statement, it announced that the operation had concluded and the recovered vessel “is now safe and under the Puntland government’s control”. During the operation, it said, 21 suspected pirates were apprehended, while operations to locate the remaining members continue. “Before the operation begun, the pirates on board the ship killed five of the crew. Among those killed were three from Pakistan, one from Myanmar and one from India,” it said. Four crew members — three Pakistanis and one Indian — were also injured, the statement added. Reuters earlier reported, citing Puntland’s state television, that the detained pirates would be brought to court. No further details of the operation were available from any of the official sources. Dawn contacted the Foreign Office (FO) for further information, but there was no immediate response. Reports of casualties Meanwhile, Ayesha Ameen, the wife of a fitter on the ship, told Dawn between sobs that there were reports of casualties among Pakistanis on the ship. She said that they were not able to confirm the names of the deceased yet, but her husband, Ameen Bin Shams, was reportedly among the injured. “We don’t know how bad the injuries are,” she said. “We are trying to establish contact with the ship’s captain on the numbers that we have. But our calls are not being answered. “As far as we know, the bodies are still on the ship, as are the injured. There is no one to tell us if they will be moved. We are going mad here,” she added. Initial reports attributed to the crew suggest that there have been five deaths and four people have been injured. Apart from Pakistanis, the vessel’s crew also included seven Indonesians, an Indian and a Sri Lankan. After its hijacking in April, months had passed with no progress either in negotiations or the payment of the ransom, said to be around $3 million, for the recovery of the hostages. The hostages were said to be victims of an “ ownership crisis ”, as it was not clearly established who owned the ship — the man previously thought to be an owner was later revealed to be more likely a middleman who hired them. Since its hijack, the crew had made several emotional videos and audio appeals , reporting that they had run out of clean water, food and medicine. Meanwhile, their families launched an international appeal, calling on foreign governments, the United Nations (UN) and the International Maritime Organisation (IMO) to take coordinated action to help secure the release of their loved ones. For its part, the FO maintained that it remained “actively engaged” to secure the release of the sailors. Last month, in a meeting with the International Maritime Organisation’s (IMO) head, Deputy Prime Minister and Foreign Minister Ishaq Dar pressed for “urgent and effective institutional intervention” for the return of the Pakistani sailors. The pirates had also contacted humanitarian Ansar Burney, who had also tried to help in resolving the matter. Ansar Burney — a former human rights minister — is the chairman of the Ansar Burney Trust, a non-profit human rights organisation working in all areas of human and civil rights worldwide. He has previously participated in efforts to free Pakistanis captured by Somali pirates. After Tuesday’s operation, the Ansar Burney Trust said in a statement that the IMO had contacted it and ensured of cooperation for the return of the injured crew and bodies to their home countries. It said it was in contact with relevant authorities, international institutions and the vessel’s crew and was making continued efforts for the return of the injured and the bodies. Somali piracy has seen a resurgence, with at least 15 attacks since April, the highest since 2013. Additional input from AFP and Reuters

items.title: Punjab forms body to review probe in Hina Javed murder case
items.description: RAWALPINDI: The Punjab government has formed a three-member high-powered committee to review the investigation in the murder case of Hina Javed in which her husband and a domestic servant have been placed on judicial remand in Adiala jail. On the other hand, the Rawalpindi police have received forensic and the final postmortem reports which showed marks of torture and other crucial evidence. According to sources, the Punjab Forensic Science Agency’s (PSFA) findings showed startling evidence of the domestic servant’s role in the gruesome murder of the woman. After the PSFA’s findings, however, police authorities are waiting for the three-member team to arrive in Rawalpindi when the case file will be presented to them. Police receive forensic and final postmortem reports which show torture, other crucial evidence The committee constituted by the provincial government consists of Additional IG Crime Control Department (CCD) Sohail Chattha, DIG Lahore Shoaib Khurram Janbaz and SSP Investigation Rawalpindi Saifullah. According to sources, the committee has been formed on the instructions of Punjab Chief Minister Maryam Nawaz Sharif, which will be headed by Mr Chattha. Sources said the committee will arrive in the city this week and will visit the crime scene and also review the investigation conducted by the local police so far. Initial postmortem examination and police report had suggested that Ms Javed’s body was found lying in a washroom of her apartment on August 21, with signs of torture as there was “strangulation mark around her neck; injury below her right lip with her nose bleeding”. The police found her body partially hanging from a washroom shower, with her hands tied behind her back and a wire noose around her neck. Ms Javed, 45, had married Faisal Imam nine months ago and was his second wife. According to sources, the committee has also contacted the family of the deceased, while the murder case was registered with Civil Lines police station. The deceased’s husband, Mr Faisal, and domestic worker Zeeshan Arshad were nominated in the murder case and were sent to Adiala Jail on judicial remand. The police had registered a murder case against the woman’s husband, who holds a doctorate degree (PhD). Her father-in-law, 78, and the domestic servant were also nominated in the case on the complaint of the victim’s brother Fahad Javed, a resident of Westridge Bazaar, Peshawar Road. It may be recalled that CPO Rawalpindi Hassan Mushtaq Sukhera had formed a special investigation team to investigate the high-profile case, but Ms Javed’s family had written letters to the Parliamentary Caucus Committee and the National Commission for Human Rights, expressing reservations about the Rawalpindi police investigation. Published in Dawn, September 30th, 2026

items.title: Poutine augmente la taille de l’armée russe pour la quatrième fois en six mois
items.description: Le décret signé lundi 28 septembre par Vladimir Poutine est entré en vigueur le jour même. Il relève de 15 500 postes les effectifs théoriques des forces armées russes par rapport au décret précédent, pour les porter à 2 441 630 hommes, dont 1 550 500 militaires Указ Президента Российской Федерации от 28.09.2026 № 700 « Об установлении штатной численности Вооруженных Сил Российской Федерации » .'> 3 . L’armée russe est la deuxième plus importante au monde après la Chine, dont l’armée compte environ 2 millions de soldats. Il s'agit du quatrième relèvement de ce type depuis le début de l'année, après des décrets signés en mars, en juin puis en juillet. Depuis mars, le nombre de postes militaires en Russie a augmenté de 47 860, soit une hausse de 3,2 % sur six mois. Ce relèvement des effectifs intervient alors que le gouvernement prépare une hausse substantielle du budget de la défense. Selon des documents gouvernementaux russes, le Kremlin prévoit de consacrer 17 100 milliards de roubles (environ 178 milliards d'euros) à la défense en 2027 Russia raises 2027 military spending by 27 %, budget documents show », Reuters , 28 septembre 2026.'> 4 . C'est 27 % de plus que l'enveloppe initialement prévue pour cette même année (13 500 milliards), et 32 % de plus par rapport à 2026 (environ 134 milliards d’euros). Tout semble indiquer que la Russie n’anticipe pas de mettre fin aux combats en Ukraine. Kiev estime que le président russe aurait déjà lancé une « mobilisation supplémentaire » afin d’augmenter substantiellement les effectifs de l’armée, notamment en se préparant à déployer 10 000 combattants nord-coréens. Selon les services de renseignement ukrainiens, l’objectif de Moscou serait de mobiliser 300 000 combattants supplémentaires d’ici fin 2027, soit le même nombre de réservistes mobilisés en septembre 2022. Le décret proclamant cette mobilisation n’a par ailleurs jamais été officiellement abrogé, ce qui signifie que les hommes mobilisés en 2022 ne peuvent être démobilisés tant que celle-ci n’est pas levée. L’article Poutine augmente la taille de l’armée russe pour la quatrième fois en six mois est apparu en premier sur Le Grand Continent .

items.title: 25 livres à lire en octobre 2026
items.description: Testez le Grand Continent . Les idées et les analyses qu’on ne trouve nulle part. Mais que vous verrez bientôt partout. Dans votre boîte mail à partir de 8 euros par mois Rebecca Shriver, A Feminine Federation ; The Interwar Campaign for Peace and European Integration , Cambridge University Press « Dans cette histoire du fédéralisme européen des années 1920 et 1930, Rebecca Shriver met en lumière un phénomène surprenant. Au-delà du récit habituel centré sur les intellectuels issus des élites masculines, les femmes et les militantes féministes de l’Union paneuropéenne, du Groupe de la Nouvelle Europe et de la Ligue internationale des femmes pour la paix et la liberté, ont façonné de nouvelles visions d’une Europe unie. Ces organisations imaginaient une fédération continentale privilégiant la coopération, la réconciliation et l’individualisme – des qualités qu’elles associaient au leadership féminin. En recadrant les échecs de l’État-nation comme le produit de systèmes “créés par les hommes”, elles proposaient des alternatives fondées sur des conceptions de la paix imprégnées d’une perspective de genre. S’appuyant sur de riches recherches d’archives, cette étude remet en question les récits conventionnels de l’intégration européenne et démontre le rôle central des femmes dans ses fondements intellectuels. Elle aborde des débats relatifs à la démocratie, à la polarisation et à la coopération internationale qui continuent de trouver un écho aujourd’hui. » Parution le 1er octobre Lire plus Tobias Becker, Heimweh nach gestern. Eine Geschichte der Nostalgie in Deutschland , Suhrkamp « Ah, le bon vieux temps ! La mode, la musique, la croissance économique… Tout était soi-disant mieux autrefois. Aujourd’hui, rien ne semble autant faire son chemin que la nostalgie d’un passé meilleur. On reproche même à la politique de jouer la carte de la nostalgie pour gagner des voix. Pourtant, la nostalgie n’est ni aussi nouvelle ni aussi mauvaise que sa réputation le laisse entendre. Tobias Becker retrace l’histoire de l’Allemagne divisée puis réunifiée à travers son rapport au passé. Comment la jeunesse des années 1960 a redécouvert les “années folles” et celle des années 1970, le rock’n’roll des années 1950 – et comment, parallèlement, le passé nazi a refait surface. Si, jusqu’en 1990, la nostalgie était considérée des deux côtés du rideau de fer comme un “phénomène capitaliste occidental”, elle semblait par la suite n’exister plus qu’en Allemagne de l’Est. Mais pourquoi le Dictionnaire mentionne-t-il l’”Ostalgie” (nostalgie de l’Est) et non la ”Westalgie” (nostalgie de l’Ouest) ? Pour Tobias Becker, la nostalgie est la clé qui permet de comprendre la société allemande. En effet, ce concept en dit plus long sur ceux qui l’utilisent que sur ceux à qui il s’applique. Qu’il s’agisse des tendances rétro dans la culture pop ou de la politique historique des partis populistes : c’est en regardant vers le passé que l’on voit qui nous sommes aujourd’hui – ou qui nous voulons être. » Parution le 1er octobre Lire plus Juan Francisco Fuentes, Marie-Angèle Orobon et José Carlos Rueda Laffond (dir.), Diccionario europeo de símbolos políticos y sociales , Taurus « Si l'être humain est, comme l'a dit le philosophe Ernst Cassirer, un animal symbolique, l'Europe est un creuset de symboles et de mythes qui ont contribué à forger son identité et son histoire. Ce dictionnaire s’attarde sur ceux qui ont façonné l’imaginaire politique et social du siècle dernier, composé d’images, de chansons, de rites et de lieux tels que le 1er mai, Stalingrad, le mur de Berlin, la croix gammée, la faucille et le marteau ou L’Internationale . Parmi la cinquantaine d’entrées contenues dans ce volume, on trouve également celles qui examinent la manière dont ont été représentés des courants, des idéologies et des mouvements sociaux tels que le féminisme, le socialisme, le fascisme, la liberté, la révolution, la mondialisation ou le progrès. Il en résulte une carte conceptuelle, visuelle et sonore fascinante de l’Europe contemporaine à travers ses symboles politiques et sociaux, ainsi que les rêves et les traumatismes qui s’y reflètent. » Parution le 1er octobre Lire plus Vincent Duclert, La philosophie contre l'antisémitisme , Puf « Survenant à la fin du XIXe siècle en France, l’affaire Dreyfus marque une rupture déterminante dans la haine des juifs. L’arbitraire politique, les attaques contre les libertés individuelles, et les menaces contre ce peuple sans État ont alors été portées à leur comble. Mais cette Affaire a aussi été la scène d’une lutte inédite contre l’antisémitisme, rendue possible grâce à l’action d’une rare mais courageuse minorité d’esprits libres, assumant les conséquences d’interventions publiques, prêts à révéler et repousser un danger mortel. Dans l’affaire Dreyfus se sont accomplis des combats premiers, modèles pour l’avenir et la survie des sociétés démocratiques. Si l’histoire de l’antisémitisme a été très largement étudiée, celle des combats contre l’antisémitisme demeure largement méconnue. Centré sur l’affaire Dreyfus au tournant du XXe siècle, ce livre questionne aussi notre temps, dominé par le défi de lutter une nouvelle fois, et avec une détermination intacte, contre ce fléau. L’importance de ces combats anciens réside dans le soubassement philosophique qui les anime. Il n’en est que plus urgent de retrouver l’histoire, de l’écrire et de la faire. » Parution le 1er octobre Lire plus Nicolas Mariot, Tuer. Comment expliquer les violences de masse, Gallimard « Guerres totales, massacres à grande échelle, génocides : les violences de masse constituent l’un des principaux legs du XXe siècle. Depuis trois décennies au moins, elles font l’objet d’un intérêt scientifique renouvelé. Le défi qu’elles posent aux chercheurs et à chacun de nous peut être résumé ainsi : comment expliquer que des personnes en apparence “ordinaires” prennent part à de tels épisodes ? Appuyée sur une douzaine d’études de cas allant de la Première Guerre mondiale au génocide des Tutsi au Rwanda, cette enquête s’intéresse aux réponses qu’historiens, sociologues ou psychologues ont apportées à la question. De quelle manière formulent-ils le problème ? Quels matériaux empiriques et quelles méthodes mobilisent-ils ? Qu’est-ce qui fait l’objet de débats ou de controverses ? Chacun des chapitres est consacré à l’examen d’une énigme concrète : pourquoi certains exécuteurs ajoutent-ils la cruauté aux meurtres ? Ou pourquoi d’autres tuent bien qu’ils reconnaissent l’humanité de leurs victimes ? Considérées ensemble, ces études dressent un bilan critique des recherches pour comprendre comment les sociétés humaines basculent dans la violence la plus extrême. » Parution le 1er octobre Lire plus Ignacio Sánchez-Cuenca, Atado y mal atado. El suicidio de las Cortes franquistas y la Transición , Catarata « Le 18 novembre 2026 marquera le cinquantième anniversaire de l’adoption de la loi sur la réforme politique (LRP), qui a permis la transformation du régime vers la démocratie. Cette loi a constitué l’élément clé de la Transition, mais aussi sa caractéristique la plus marquante d’un point de vue comparatif. La démocratie n’est pas née d’une rupture, mais d’une réforme des lois fondamentales qui faisaient office de constitution franquiste. L’une des grandes énigmes de la Transition a été le comportement des députés des Cortes franquistes, qui ont voté en faveur d’une loi qui, dans la pratique, mettait fin à leurs positions de pouvoir et ouvrait la voie à des élections démocratiques et à une période constituante. Kupchan, qu’elles seront en mesure de guider le monde à travers la transition à venir et, à terme, de ramener l’arc de l’histoire vers la liberté. » Parution le 20 octobre Lire plus Antonio Scurati, Storie di donne e uomini in lotta per la democrazia, Feltrinelli « “Qu’aurais-je fait à leur place ? Voilà le dilemme. Aucune autre question n’a vraiment de sens lorsque nous entamons une correspondance avec une humanité lointaine, tourmentée, une vie étrangère, lorsque nous entrons en résonance avec une époque où quelques personnes solitaires ont trouvé la force d’invoquer la justice au milieu des ravages, de témoigner de leur foi en la démocratie face au triomphe de la dictature, leur attachement à la vérité face au règne du mensonge.” C’est à partir de ce dilemme, qui interroge les moments les plus marquants et les plus dramatiques du XXe siècle européen, qu’Antonio Scurati raconte l’existence extraordinaire de femmes et d’hommes qui, en résistant aux fascismes, aux totalitarismes, à la violence du pouvoir sous toutes ses formes, ont défendu les valeurs de la démocratie et, en les réaffirmant, ont peu à peu fait valoir de nouveaux droits : ceux des travailleurs, des femmes, des homosexuels, des malades, des étudiants, de l’environnement. De Sandro Pertini à Anna Politkovskaïa, de Franco Basaglia à Livia Bottardi et Manlio Milani, de Gisèle Halimi à Alexander Langer, des femmes et des hommes qui ont élargi les horizons démocratiques au point, dans certains cas, de payer leur fidélité tenace par la prison, l’exil, voire la vie. À travers leurs conquêtes – surtout celles qui sont imparfaites ou trahies –, la démocratie redevient un combat vivant, quotidien. Si bien qu’après nous être demandé “Qu’aurais-je fait à leur place ?”, nous nous interrogeons désormais : que puis-je faire, aujourd’hui, à ma place ? » Parution le 20 octobre Lire plus Teemu Ruskola, The Unmaking of the Chinese Working Class : How Communism Built a Capitalist Superpower , Verso « Depuis les réformes de la fin des années 1970, la Chine a connu une croissance à un rythme extraordinaire. Cette transformation n’a pas signifié un retrait de l’État de l’économie. En effet, ce sont les fondements communistes de la Chine qui ont rendu possible ce développement stupéfiant. Pourtant, parallèlement, ces réformes ont vu la Chine renoncer à l’idée d’égalité, démantelant ainsi la classe ouvrière que la révolution avait forgée. Le récit de Teemu Ruskola met l’accent sur l’organisation de la terre et du travail comme clé de compréhension de l’essor de la Chine, expliquant comment leur marchandisation a remodelé non seulement l’État-nation chinois, mais aussi le capitalisme mondial lui-même. Remettant en cause les discours dominants sur le développement économique, cet ouvrage démontre en quoi l’évolution du capitalisme d’État chinois s’écarte à la fois du passage de l’Angleterre du féodalisme au capitalisme et des transformations post-socialistes de l’Union soviétique. Mettant en évidence les limites planétaires du développement, l’ouvrage est un appel urgent à repenser notre rapport au travail et à la terre, à la production et à la nature. » Parution le 20 octobre Lire plus Nicholas Mulder, The Age of Confiscation ; Making and Taking Property in the Creation of the Modern World , Allen Lane « L’expropriation – le transfert forcé des droits de propriété – est généralement associée aux dictateurs, aux pays instables et aux révolutions violentes. Mais, en réalité, elle a fait partie intégrante de l’histoire politique et économique de l’Occident, permettant tant l’abolition du servage et de l’esclavage que l’industrialisation, l’essor et le déclin des empires coloniaux, ainsi que l’expansion de l’État-providence. Pour le meilleur ou pour le pire, une grande partie de notre monde moderne s’est construite grâce à l’acquisition coercitive de biens. Dans cette histoire internationale novatrice de l’expropriation, Nicholas Mulder trace un parcours captivant du XVIIIe siècle à nos jours, allant de la Révolution française à la guerre russo-ukrainienne, des compagnies coloniales aux empires ferroviaires, de la vente des terres de l’Église à la nationalisation du pétrole, et de la confiscation des brevets au gel des avoirs sur le marché de l’eurodollar. Il montre comment toutes sortes de mouvements politiques – libéraux et nationalistes, socialistes et fascistes, impérialistes et anticolonialistes – ont à la fois dissous et redistribué les droits de propriété. La réussite de la construction de l’État ne dépendait pas de l’élimination de l’État confiscatoire, mais de la maîtrise de ses pouvoirs et de leur réorientation vers de nouvelles fins. S'appuyant sur un large éventail de sources et de données issues de l'histoire, de la politique et de l'économie, Nicholas Mulder propose une histoire audacieuse retraçant la manière dont la propriété a été créée puis démantelée, transférée puis convertie, volée puis restituée. The Age of Confiscation révèle à quel point l'expropriation a marqué notre passé récent et comment, dans un contexte de concurrence géopolitique croissante, d'inégalités grandissantes et de changement climatique, elle marquera notre avenir. » Parution le 29 octobre Lire plus L’article 25 livres à lire en octobre 2026 est apparu en premier sur Le Grand Continent .

items.title: United Arab Emirates: A Year On, Critic Remains in Detention
items.description: Click to expand Image Samuel Peter Oyay © Private (Beirut) – A South Sudanese political commentator remains in prison in the United Arab Emirates (UAE) without charge a year after his arrest, Human Rights Watch said today. Emirati authorities have not disclosed the legal basis for the arrest of the commentator, Samuel Peter Oyay, to his family. Oyay fled South Sudan in 2014, fearing for his safety. He moved to the UAE and had been running a private business there. While in the UAE, Oyay had written regularly for independent South Sudan-focused platforms, accusing its government of corruption that benefits the elite. The UAE and South Sudan have strengthened their bilateral relations in recent years. In 2025, President Salva Kiir visited the UAE at least three times. “The UAE government’s zero-tolerance policy toward peaceful criticism is increasingly targeting critics of Abu Dhabi’s foreign allies who live in the UAE,” said Joey Shea, senior United Arab Emirates researcher at Human Rights Watch. “Emirati authorities should immediately release Samuel Oyay, who has been held for a year without charge.” In the last article published before his detention, on September 21, 2025, Oyay criticized the trial of Riek Machar, the suspended first vice president and leader of the main opposition party, as a ploy by President Kiir to weaken a rival rather than deliver justice. On September 22, 2026, the president dissolved the transitional government, most likely to pave the way for elections, while Machar and other key opposition figures’ trial was ongoing. On September 30, 2025, Emirati security forces in civilian clothes arrested Oyay in front of his four children at their home in Dubai after searching his home for two hours, an informed source told Human Rights Watch. During Oyay’s arrest, Emirati security forces did not show his family a warrant, or inform him of the charges or the legal basis for his arrest, the source said. UAE authorities allowed Oyay to call his family two weeks later, the source said, but did not disclose his whereabouts to his relatives for five months. On February 24, 2026, Oyay told the informed source that he was being held in al-Wathba prison. He was moved to another prison on March 3, the source said. Prison authorities allow Oyay one short phone call per week. Oyay’s family received a call from UAE authorities on March 2 authorizing a visit for March 3, but when they tried to visit him, the authorities told them that he had been moved to another prison that day, the source said. Emirati authorities called the family again on July 1 to schedule a visit for July 8, when they were finally able to visit, and have not been able to visit since. Human Rights Watch has previously documented that South Sudanese critics in exile have been disappeared or forcefully returned with support of the South Sudan government. In April 2024, a UAE company signed a €12 billion (US$12.9 billion) oil-for-cash deal with South Sudan. Most of South Sudan’s crude is refined in Fujairah, one of the UAE’s seven emirates. But South Sudan’s oil exports have been significantly impacted by the war in neighboring Sudan. Human Rights Watch has documented the UAE’s longstanding record of arbitrary detention, enforced disappearances, torture, denial of medical care, prolonged solitary confinement, and continued detention beyond completed sentences. Article 48 of the UAE’s criminal law of procedure states that detainees should be taken before the public prosecutor within 48 hours. The UAE’s 2003 State Security Apparatus Law, however, gives state security officers wide powers to hold detainees for lengthy periods without any judicial scrutiny. Article 28 of the state security law, read in conjunction with article 14, allows the head of the state security apparatus to detain a person for 106 days “if he has sufficient reasonable causes to make him believe” that the person is involved in, among other things, “activities that undermine the state … or jeopardize national unity,” “activities deemed harmful to the economy,” or anything that “could undermine, weaken the position of, stir animosity against or undermine trust in the State.” The state security apparatus law inherently violates international human rights law including article 14(5) of the Arab Charter on Human Rights, which states that “anyone arrested or detained on a criminal charge shall be brought promptly before a judge or other officer authorized by law to exercise judicial power and shall be entitled to trial within a reasonable time or to release.” The UAE ratified the Arab Charter in 2008. The UAE should ensure that in its law and practice, every detainee is taken within 48 hours before an independent judge to consider the legality and necessity of their detention and whether they should be immediately released, Human Rights Watch said. “The UAE’s continued detention of Oyay shows authorities’ relentless attack on human rights against its own citizens and residents who make the UAE their home,” Shea said. “The UAE isn't content with silencing their own critics but is also doing the same for its allies.”

items.title: Iran says it receives US response to latest proposal as Washington pulls out of Iraq
items.description: By Ahmed Rasheed, Jana Choukeir and Andrew Mills BAGHDAD/DUBAI, Sept 30 (Reuters) - Iran said on Wednesday it had received a US response to its latest proposal to resurrect the collapsed ceasefire in the Gulf, days after President Donald Trump said he had rejected it. Iran's allies were celebrating on Wednesday after Washington withdrew the last of its forces from neighbouring Iraq, where 4,500 US troops died in the biggest US war of the century. More than 200,000 Iraqi civilians were killed in chaos unleashed after US forces toppled dictator Saddam Hussein in 2003.

items.title: Imran’s sisters ‘on hunger strike for two days’, cousin claims
items.description: ISLAMABAD: Three sisters of Imran Khan — Aleema Khan, Uzma Khan and Noreen Niazi — have been on hunger strike for the last 48 hours, according to Imran Khan’s cousin Qasim Zaman, who reached Adiala Jail on Tuesday to meet the former prime minister but was not allowed to do so. Similarly, interim PTI Chairman Barrister Gohar Ali Khan and Mr Khan’s lawyers also reached Adiala jail, but they were also not allowed to meet their client. Mr Zaman alleged that the sisters of Imran Khan started their hunger strike due to misbehaviour with them during their detention. Reports of their being on hunger strike had been circulating, but this was the first time that a family member had confirmed the claims. PTI lawyer Awais Younas Chaudhry told Dawn that lawyers and a family member reached Adiala jail at 2pm and waited there till 4:30pm, but they were not allowed to meet the PTI founder. “It is tragic that the jail administration has been violating orders of the Islamabad High Court and Supreme Court of Pakistan but courts appear to be helpless,” he said. Published in Dawn, September 30th, 2026

items.title: ‘La Bohème’ en la Puerta del Sol
items.description: Cuando Benoît llama a la puerta de la buhardilla reclamando el alquiler, Marcello y Rodolfo, los alegres protagonistas de La Bohème de Puccini , le vacilan y lo emborrachan hasta que se libran del pago, en un divertido desacato a la ley y a la propiedad privada que fue muy celebrado por los burgueses que ocupaban los palcos del Teatro Regio de Turín el día de su estreno, el 1 de febrero de 1896. Muchos de ellos serían caseros como Benoît, pero se reconocían en la picaresca de Rodolfo. Así ha sucedido siempre, incluida la última vez que se representó en el Teatro Real de Madrid. Esta ópera inmortal sobre perroflautas que no pueden permitirse un cuchitril en París siempre es aplaudida por públicos con la hipoteca amortizada. Seguir leyendo

items.title: Israel Elejalde y Javier Cámara, hermanados por el punk: “Es un fracaso que haya gente que crea que recuperar el franquismo sea una forma de contestación”
items.description: La propuesta inicial para esta entrevista era encontrarnos en alguno de los garitos punk que todavía quedan en Madrid, pero ya casi no quedan en zonas céntricas de la ciudad. Igual que los propios madrileños , la mayoría están confinados en la periferia para sobrevivir a la especulación. Así que nos conformamos con agua, infusiones y café en una sala de la Nave 10 de Matadero Madrid, contigua al escenario donde Israel Elejalde y Javier Cámara ensayan la historia de dos hermanos punk que formaron en los noventa una banda llamada Verborrea. Es la nueva obra del dramaturgo y director Pablo Remón, titulada también Verborrea , que se estrena este jueves y en la que comparten reparto con Marta Nieto y Emilio Tomé. Seguir leyendo

items.title: Una expedición hispano-argentina viajará a los Andes para comprobar si es real un geoglifo localizado por Google Earth
items.description: El diccionario de la lengua española explica que un geoglifo es una “figura de gran tamaño en laderas o en grandes llanuras, especialmente de pueblos prehistóricos, grabada directamente sobre el terreno o realizada con piedras”. De todos los que se han localizado en el mundo, los más famosos son los de Nazca (Perú), declarados Patrimonio de la Humanidad. Solo son visibles desde montañas circundantes o desde el aire, lo que les proporciona una vitola de misterio. Ahora, un grupo de investigadores de Argentina y España van a estudiar una estructura que podría ser un geoglifo localizado el año pasado sobre los 3.000 metros de altura en la cordillera andina del Tigre (Argentina) y que fue descubierto por el andinista Carlos Gobbi cuando consultaba Google Earth. Una expedición conjunta intentará analizarlo in situ el próximo diciembre. Seguir leyendo
